newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Arb cargoes take naphtha down.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Arb cargoes take naphtha down.

text.p: Talk of arbitrage cargoes from the West shook the naphtha market with Singapore barrels shedding nearly 70 cents, traders said on Friday.
Traders said 150,000 tonnes of Algerian naphtha was due to arrive in the East in April and a Mexican cargo was also being offered in the market.
"Occasionally from Venezuela, but I have never seen a cargo from Mexico," a trader said.
"The market is so weak...anybody can use this (arbitrage offers) to bring the market down," a trader said.
Arbitrage talk has pressured down the East-West naphtha spreads to $22-$23 per tonne, down from over $30 last week, a trader said.
But the arbitrage has already closed and traders doubted the arrival of more cargoes.

Singapore naphtha swaps for March extended their losses overnight to $22.90/$23.10 per barrel from $23.55/$23.75, while Japan's open-spec for second-half April lost $5.50 per tonne overnight to settle at $226.00/$228.00.

Some traders thought there was more room to the fall while others said prices should have already found a floor and should stabilise at these levels as these arbitrage cargoes "can easily be absorbed".
They said they still saw demand in April from South Korea, Thailand and China although Japan was mostly already covered.

State-owned Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) concluded the sale of 2.7 million tonnes of full-range naphtha on term between March 1997-February 1998 to buyers in Japan, South Korea and India, industry sources said.
They said KPC renewed the contracts with 10 buyers from Japan for 1.5 million tonnes and four from South Korea for 900,000 tonnes.
It signed a new contract with India's Reliance Industries for 300,000 tonnes, the sources said.
Reliance was seeking supplies to for its 700,000 tonnes-per-year petrochemical plant, which started up in December and was due to operate at full capacity in March.
KPC set a record price of $13.50 per tonne over Mideast spot quotes on a free-on-board basis for the supplies.

Gasoline moved up in thin talks. Only one aggresive buyer improved the 92-octane unleaded grade bid intraday from $27.40 to $27.75 where it found a seller for the 50,000 barrels lifting March 7-21 and concluded the deal.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
